## Description

Rank industries using multi-year relative returns, identify extreme long-term underperformers, and only consider them when valuation is attractive and fundamental deterioration is not accelerating. Add confirmation such as stabilizing margins or earnings, diversify across industries, and enter gradually. Compare the valuation-confirmed strategy with a pure long-horizon industry-reversal baseline.

## Where it may fit

Long-horizon contrarian opportunities after sustained industry underperformance; weak when relative weakness reflects permanent structural decline or rapid technological disruption.

## Vehicles

Sector/industry ETFs or diversified baskets of liquid stocks classified by industry.

## Required data

Multi-year industry and security returns, point-in-time valuation ratios, industry-level fundamentals, earnings/margin trends, corporate actions, and realistic turnover/cost assumptions.

## Caveats

Published work reports long-term industry or market reversal, but the effect may be unstable and is not proof that every losing industry will rebound. Valuation confirmation is a proposed filter, not an established guarantee. Guard against survivorship, look-ahead, sector classification changes, value traps, and overly long drawdown periods.
